media.alt: International Education Conference-Hamida Khuhro praises AKU-IED for promoting quality education

content.text: The opening ceremony of the international conference on 'Quality in Education: Teaching and Leadership in Challenging Times' was held at Aga Khan University (AKU) on Tuesday, Feb 21, 2006. Dr Hamida Khuhro, Minister for Education and Literacy, Government of Sindh, was the chief guest at the ceremony.

The three-day conference was organised by Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED). Educationists from Pakistan, India, East Africa, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Malaysia, Poland, UK, US and Canada are participating in the conference.

Lauding AKU-IED's work, Dr Khuhro said that since its inception, the Institute has been engaged in developing and delivering quality programmes in teacher education, educational leadership, early childhood education and development, environment education, inclusive education, gender education, citizenship education and health education. She further added that the series of policy dialogues conducted by AKU-IED during the past three years on key issues in education with government and other agencies had been remarkable. "These dialogues have enabled policy makers in identifying problems, designing and analysing research and making policy recommendations."

In her keynote address, the Director of the Institute for Development Studies and Practices, Quetta, Dr Quratulain Bakhtiari, said that leadership was built by integrating with people, not by isolating educational institutions from the people. "The formal education system does not consider the experiences outside the schools as an educational development process. In fact, schools negate all that goes on in the communities and in the lives of the ordinary people or in the isolated communities, thus limiting all the opportunities of developing leadership opportunities through an educational process."

Earlier in his welcome address, AKU President Shamsh Kassim-Lakha introduced the chief guest and welcomed the delegates of the conference. Pointing out the fact that in many low-income countries, teachers do not meet even the minimum required standards for their profession, President Kassim-Lakha recounted the factors that encouraged AKU to concentrate on education of teachers, school heads as well as policymakers. "The impact of the Institute and its Professional Development Centres (PDC) have been far reaching. Graduates of AKU-IED return to their schools of origin well-equipped to enhance not only their own pedagogical skills but more so those of their colleagues as well as address challenges in school systems," he added.

In his opening remarks, AKU-IED Director, Dr Muhammad Memon welcomed the guests and said that quality in education could not be realised without improving the quality of teachers, curriculum, assessment, teaching-learning process and enabling environment. "The role of teachers and other educational personnel in providing quality education needs to be recognised and their working conditions and status also need to be improved."

Elaborating on AKU-IED's research work, he said AKU-IED was actively engaged in conducting research in education with special emphasis on school improvement and teacher education. "To date, 62 research studies by the faculty and 243 MEd dissertations have been completed. Several consultancy reports have also been prepared."

Dr David Taylor, Acting Provost AKU, also highlighted the role of AKU-IED in improving the quality of education in developing countries. He also emphasised the relationship between the quality of education and research.

The Chair of the International Conference Committee and Head of Research and Policy Studies, AKU-IED, Dr Anjum Halai, in her concluding remarks, said such conferences were a significant voice in the debate for quality in education. "Significant, because it is rare if not unusual for academic gatherings to be arranged in this part of the world; gatherings, which are focused on issues pertaining to quality education with specific reference to the developing world."
